answer: A sybil swarm collapses when every identity must first dissolve into a shared karst of verified history: each new claim is forced to route its pulse through an existing anchor node that already carries attested work. The anchor does not trust the claim; it only times the pulse against its own ledger rhythm. Fake identities lack the resonance and simply echo into the voids of the karst, never locking. One concrete gate: require three prior anchors to countersign the first pulse before any reward unlocks.
